component.name: FujiNet Go Apple II
component.summary: Self-contained Apple II with built-in FujiNet

description.p: An Apple II with FujiNet built in: mount disk images from TNFS servers or the local SD folder, configure everything through the embedded FujiNet web UI, and play with automatic gamepad support driving the analog paddles.

Emulation is provided by AppleWin, with FujiNet attached as a SmartPort card in slot 7 -- the slot the Apple //e autostart ROM scans before the Disk ][, so the machine boots straight into FujiNet's CONFIG.

screenshot.caption: FujiNet CONFIG running on the emulated Apple II

description.p: Settings now has a Scanlines toggle in place of Smooth scaling -- turning scanlines on also turns on smoothing, since the two look best together. Power Cycle now restarts the FujiNet runtime along with the machine, matching a real peripheral card's own reboot. Fixed an occasional hang on quit when FujiNet's runtime was still shutting down. The FujiNet web admin now binds 64001 instead of 8000. For firmware developers: a new tools/fujinet/update-fujinet-firmware.sh script bumps the pinned fujinet-firmware submodule, and FN_DEBUG=1 builds libfujinet.so with full debug info for gdb.
The macOS bundle now ships its own app icon (rendered from the same Android launcher art as every other frontend's) instead of falling back to the generic AppKit icon.

Release artifacts now embed the Apple II system ROMs, so the flatpak, macOS bundle and Windows build all boot out of the box -- following AppleWin's own long-standing precedent. The ROM-less configuration (WITH_APPLE_ROMS=OFF) remains fully supported for anyone who cannot embed Apple's firmware under their own policy, and a build made that way now reports clearly when no ROMs have been imported yet instead of a generic startup failure.
First release of the Apple II desktop app: AppleWin's libretro core driven on a vsync-phase-locked emulator thread, with the FujiNet firmware built in-process and joined over SmartPort-over-SLIP.
